title: Sell Mineral Rights in Axis, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Axis, AL | Mobile County
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Axis, AL? Get a hedged, activity-based cash offer for Mobile County acreage close to the Citronelle Field trend.
heroLead: Axis sits along the Mobile River corridor north of the city of Mobile, inside the broader ring of Mobile County land that saw leasing activity fan out from the 1955 Citronelle Field discovery a few miles to the west.
intro: The unincorporated community of Axis grew up around river and rail industry rather than oil production, but the mineral estate under much of the surrounding land was leased and sometimes drilled during the decades that followed Citronelle's discovery. Ownership here tends to be a mix of small parcels tied to industrial or timber land and family-held tracts that never saw a rig, and we buy both kinds of interest.

sections.heading: Axis and the Citronelle trend
paragraphs: Citronelle Field, once the largest onshore oil field east of the Mississippi River, sits a short distance west of Axis, and secondary leasing swept through much of Mobile County in the years after its discovery. Axis itself was never a core producing area, but nearby permit activity and the general Norphlet-Smackover trend running through this part of Mobile County still shape how a local mineral interest gets valued.

sections.heading: Industrial land and split mineral ownership
paragraphs: A lot of surface acreage around Axis has shifted toward industrial, rail, and river-access use over the decades, and when that happens the mineral estate is frequently carved out and retained separately by the prior owner or their heirs. It's common for us to work with someone whose family sold surface land generations ago but kept the minerals, unaware the reservation was ever recorded.

sections.heading: Confirming ownership through Mobile County records
paragraphs: Mobile County's probate and deed records are the reference point for confirming a mineral reservation or inheritance tied to Axis-area land. We pull that history as part of every offer, and if the interest passed through several generations without a formal partition, we'll help identify each heir's actual share before finalizing anything.

faqs.question: Is Axis considered part of the Citronelle Field itself?
faqs.answer: Not the core field, but it sits within the broader Norphlet-Smackover trend that runs through this part of Mobile County, so nearby activity and permit history still inform value for local tracts.

faqs.question: The surface near our family's Axis property was sold for industrial use decades ago. Do we still own the minerals?
faqs.answer: Often yes, if the mineral estate was reserved in the original sale. We help confirm that through Mobile County deed and probate records before making an offer.

faqs.question: What if I only inherited a small fractional share?
faqs.answer: That's typical for Axis-area interests passed through multiple generations, and we regularly buy fractional shares once your percentage is documented.
